concepts.name: Features, labels and examples
concepts.summary: Identify rows as examples, columns as features, and the target column as the label in a tabular dataset.

concepts.name: Supervised versus unsupervised learning
concepts.summary: Explain how learning from labelled data (prediction) differs from finding structure in unlabelled data.

concepts.name: Classification versus regression
concepts.summary: Decide whether a problem predicts a category or a numeric value based on the target.

concepts.name: Model fitting and prediction
concepts.summary: Describe training as learning parameters from data and prediction as applying the fitted model to new examples.

concepts.name: Train and test split
concepts.summary: Explain why a model is fitted on one part of the data and evaluated on held-out data.

concepts.name: Accuracy as a basic metric
concepts.summary: Define accuracy as the fraction of correct predictions and compute it from predictions and true labels.

concepts.name: Overfitting intuition
concepts.summary: Describe how a model can do well on training data yet poorly on new data because it memorized noise.

misconceptions.text: A model with high training accuracy is necessarily a good model.
Machine learning always needs labelled data.
Any problem with numbers in the target column is a regression problem, even when the numbers are class codes.

concepts.name: Feature scaling
concepts.summary: Apply standardization or min-max scaling and know which methods depend on feature scale.

concepts.name: Confusion matrix metrics
concepts.summary: Build a confusion matrix and compute precision, recall and F1 from true/false positives and negatives.

concepts.name: Encoding categorical features
concepts.summary: Convert categorical columns to numeric form using one-hot or ordinal encoding as appropriate.

concepts.name: Hyperparameters versus parameters
concepts.summary: Distinguish values learned from data from settings such as tree depth or k that are chosen beforehand.

concepts.name: Decision tree splitting
concepts.summary: Explain how a tree chooses feature thresholds that reduce impurity such as Gini or entropy, and read a fitted tree.

concepts.name: k-nearest neighbours prediction
concepts.summary: Apply kNN by finding the k closest examples under a distance and voting or averaging their labels.

concepts.name: Missing value handling
concepts.summary: Apply simple imputation strategies such as median or most frequent and recognise their effect.

concepts.name: k-means clustering procedure
concepts.summary: Run k-means by alternating assignment to nearest centroid and centroid updates until convergence.

misconceptions.text: Decision trees and kNN need feature scaling in the same way.
Accuracy is a reliable metric on any dataset, including heavily imbalanced ones.
Encoding categories as integers 1, 2, 3 is always harmless for distance-based models.

concepts.name: Cross-validation
concepts.summary: Use k-fold and stratified cross-validation to estimate generalization and compare models.

concepts.name: Bias-variance tradeoff
concepts.summary: Analyse errors as bias and variance and use learning curves to diagnose underfitting or overfitting.

concepts.name: Regularization
concepts.summary: Apply penalties or complexity limits such as L1, L2, pruning and depth limits to reduce variance.

concepts.name: Random forests and bagging
concepts.summary: Explain and apply bagging with random feature subsets to reduce the variance of trees.

concepts.name: Data leakage
concepts.summary: Identify how information from test data or the target leaks into training and prevent it with pipelines.

concepts.name: ROC curve and AUC
concepts.summary: Interpret ROC curves and AUC and relate decision thresholds to the precision-recall trade-off.

concepts.name: Hyperparameter search
concepts.summary: Tune hyperparameters with grid or random search inside cross-validation.

concepts.name: Feature engineering
concepts.summary: Construct and select features such as ratios, interactions and aggregates, and judge their usefulness.

misconceptions.text: Scaling or imputing on the full dataset before splitting is fine because it uses no labels.
A higher ROC AUC means the model is better at every threshold and for any class balance.
Adding more trees to a random forest causes it to overfit more.

concepts.name: Gradient boosting mechanics
concepts.summary: Analyse how boosting fits trees sequentially to the gradient of the loss and how learning rate, depth and rounds interact.

concepts.name: SVM margins and kernels
concepts.summary: Explain maximum margin, the role of C and support vectors, and how kernels such as RBF enable nonlinear boundaries.

concepts.name: PCA and variance explained
concepts.summary: Interpret principal components as directions of maximal variance and choose the number of components.

concepts.name: Handling class imbalance
concepts.summary: Evaluate class weights, resampling and threshold moving against the cost of errors.

concepts.name: Model comparison and selection
concepts.summary: Judge models using nested cross-validation, variance across folds and metrics suited to the problem.

concepts.name: Choosing k and cluster validity
concepts.summary: Evaluate cluster quality and the choice of k using silhouette, inertia and stability.

concepts.name: Feature importance and interpretation
concepts.summary: Compare impurity-based and permutation importance and interpret model behaviour while recognising correlated-feature pitfalls.

concepts.name: Probability calibration
concepts.summary: Assess whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies and choose a calibration method.

misconceptions.text: Oversampling before the train-test split is a valid way to balance classes.
Impurity-based feature importance reliably shows which features truly drive predictions.
PCA components are always the most predictive directions for the target.

concepts.name: Designing evaluation protocols
concepts.summary: Design validation schemes such as grouped or time-based splits that match deployment conditions and avoid optimistic estimates.

concepts.name: Cost-sensitive decision framing
concepts.summary: Translate error costs and constraints into metrics and thresholds and justify the choice.

concepts.name: Diagnosing distribution shift
concepts.summary: Detect and evaluate covariate and concept drift and judge responses such as retraining or reweighting.

concepts.name: Boosting regularization and tuning strategy
concepts.summary: Critique and choose boosting settings including shrinkage, subsampling and early stopping under a compute budget.

concepts.name: Ensembling and stacking design
concepts.summary: Construct stacked or blended ensembles with out-of-fold predictions and judge when they add value.

concepts.name: Pipeline and feature system design
concepts.summary: Create reproducible pipelines that couple preprocessing, features and models safely and prevent train-serve skew.

concepts.name: Uncertainty and statistical comparison
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether metric differences between models are real using resampling and appropriate tests.

concepts.name: Choosing classical versus deep methods
concepts.summary: Justify model family choice for a tabular problem given data size, interpretability, latency and maintenance.

misconceptions.text: Random k-fold cross-validation is a valid estimate of performance for any dataset, including time series or grouped data.
Stacking more diverse models always improves performance.
A small difference in cross-validated score between two models proves one is better.
